Zak Macey Group 4 Each element is covered in the weekly sessions, using the BOOSE library source code as an example. I will discuss how I implemented the more difficult elements (like the parser, implementing loops etc.) Keep your progress up to date below. Put "DONE" after each section, when you have done it. The number in brackets represents the component that each element contributes to. Checkpoint 1 Version Control (1) At least two documented commits to provided on GitHub Classroom BEFORE 12pm 7th October. At least 5 documented commits. Readme.md file filled in correctly. 2 Unit Tests for basic drawing commands above (1) Unit Test for moveto command (variables storing pen position are correct) Unit Test for drawTo command (variables storing pen position are correct) Unit Test for a multiline program. 3 XML Comments/documentation produced (1) Fully documented with XML comments and Documentation web site produced 4 Exception Handling (1) 5 Library (DLL) installed and working with reasonable user interface (2) Form interface with program window, output window and run button BOOSE DLL library installed call about method and display returned information in output/debug window you can use System.Diagnostics to output to the debug window 6 Basic drawing commands of the library are implemented (2) Moveto, circle, rect, pencolour, write. Unrestricted drawing programs can be run (1unrestrictedDrawing.boose) You MUST fill in the this form before submission and submit your zipped up project to myBeckett Read the hand in instructions on myBeckett carefully to ensure you are submitting everything correctly, as if you don't you may be subject to a penalty. Final Submission 1 Further Version Control (1) You must continue to use VC to a professional standard with frequent and clear commits Your Readme.md must be up to date 2 Use of Interfaces (1) Interfaces to be used for all classes where appropriate 3 Further Unit Testing (1) Tests for full program all of the facilities completed in 5,6 and 7 below It is up to you how design your tests (i.e. one test per facility or one test testing many but they must be clearly documented with XML comments) 4 Design Patterns (1) Use of factory Design Pattern for command creation Use of Singleton Design Pattern Demonstrate the use of another design pattern of your choice (for 5,6 and 7 you can click the links to see the example BOOSE programs that must be run, these are in your Portfolio. You must run the unrestricted programs and replace the image already there with an image of your BOOSE Interpreter running the BOOSE programs. You may show further programs in your portfolio.) 5 Replaced variables (2) * Int Real Array 6 Replaced if, while, for (2) * While For If else 7 Replaced Methods (2) * 8 Additional (web version, text-based version, extension to BOOSE itself, etc, discuss with your tutor) (2) * You must rewrite the functionality and not try and "hack the system". I've tried to make it so you can't but who knows, either way, you've been told. You MUST fill in this form whilst recording your YouTube Video AND submit it to myBeckett Read the hand in instructions on myBeckett carefully to ensure you are submitting everything correctly, as if you don't you may be subject to a penalty. api/BooseASEzm.html.summary: Namespace BooseASEzm Classes AppArray Represents an array variable that stores multiple values of the same type (int or real). Supports indexed access for storing and retrieving values. AppCall Command to invoke a previously defined method with arguments. Evaluates arguments (literals or variables) and passes them to the method. AppCanvas Represents a canvas that supports basic drawing operations such as circles, rectangles, lines, and text with customizable colors. Implements the BOOSE.ICanvas interface. AppCircle The app circle class is responsible for calling the unrestricted version of the circle method it inherits from the commandoneparameter class the radius of the circle is provided as a parameter AppCommandFactory The AppCommandFactory class is responsible for creating specific command objects based on the provided command type. Inherits from the BOOSE.CommandFactory class. AppFor For loop command that iterates a counter variable from a start value to an end value with a specified step. Automatically manages the counter variable and supports both ascending and descending loops. AppIf AppInt Integer variable command that supports variable declarations, assignments, and expression evaluation. Handles both simple value assignments and complex arithmetic expressions. AppMethod Method definition command that allows creating reusable code blocks with parameters and return values. Methods store their return value in a variable with the same name as the method. AppMoveTo The AppMoveTo class is responsible for moving the position of the pen on the canvas. It inherits from the CommandTwoParameters class where the x and y values are supplied as parameters. AppParser Custom parser that extends BOOSE.Parser to support control structures and methods. Parses programs with if/else statements, while loops, for loops, and method definitions. AppPeek Peek command to get an array element and store it in a variable. Usage: peek x = nums 5 peek y = prices 3 AppPoke Command to set a value at a specific index in an array. Supports both integer and real arrays. AppReal Unrestricted real (double/decimal) variable command. Handles variable declarations like: real x = 10.5 AppRect The appRect class is responsible for calling the unrestricted version of the rect command it inherits the command two parameters class the height and width are provided as parameters AppStoredProgram Custom StoredProgram that bypasses BOOSE restrictions. Inherits from BOOSE.StoredProgram but allows unrestricted commands. AppWhile While loop command. Usage: while condition commands... end while AppWrite Unrestricted write command that displays text, variables, and expressions on the canvas. Inherits from CommandOneParameter to handle the parameter parsing. Form1 The main form of the application. It initializes the canvas, command factory, stored program, and parser, and provides functionality for interacting with the canvas via user input. MethodParameter Represents a parameter in a method definition with a type and name.
